  1669	\begin{lemma}
  1670	\label{lem:qld-unitary}
  1671	There exists a function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)$ (where $\delta_S$ is defined in \Cref{lem:qld-4-7}) and unitaries $V_\alice$ acting on registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ and $V_\bob$ acting on $\bob \bob' \bob''$ such that 
  1672	\begin{enumerate}
  1673		\item There exists a state $\ket{\aux}$ on registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ such that
  1674		\[
  1675			\left \| V_\alice \otimes V_\bob \ket{\hat{\psi}}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''} - \ket{\aux}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\alice'' \bob''} \right \|^2 \leq \delta_\qld.
  1676		\]
  1677		
  1678		\item For all $W \in \{X,Z\}, h \in \F_q^\nqubits$
  1679		\begin{align*}
  1680			V_\alice \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \Big)_{\alice} \, V_\alice^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \\
  1681			 V_\bob \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h  \Big)_{\bob}\, V_\bob^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''}
  1682		\end{align*}
  1683		where the $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\aux}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\alice'' \bob''}$. 
  1684	\end{enumerate}
  1685	\end{lemma}
  1686	
  1687	\begin{proof}
  1688	
  1689	Define the linear map
  1690	\[
  1691		V_\alice = \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)))_{\alice ''}\;,
  1692	\]
  1693	where the $\tau^X(\cdot),\tau^Z(\cdot)$ act on $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$. (Also note that the argument of $\tau^X$ is $\coded(g_Z)$ and the argument of $\tau^Z$ is $\coded(g_X)$.) We verify the unitarity of $V_\alice$:
  1694	\begin{align*}
  1695		V_\alice V_\alice^\dagger &= \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) )_{\alice ''} \\
  1696		&= \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Id_{\alice ''} \\
  1697		&= \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''}
  1698	\end{align*}
  1699	where in the first line we used that the measurement $\{ \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \}$  is projective and in the second line we used that the $\tau^Z$ and $\tau^X$ observables are self-inverse. The unitary $V_\bob$ is defined analogously.
  1700	
  1701	Let $\{e_j\}_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}}$ denote the self-dual basis for $\F_q$ over $\F_2$ specified in \Cref{sec:subfields}, and let $\tilde{W}^j$ be the observables introduced in~\eqref{eq:def-tildewj}. Conjugating the observable $\tilde{W}^j$ acting on the registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ by the unitary $V_\alice$ we get
  1702	\begin{align*}
  1703		&V_\alice \, \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \, V_\alice^\dagger \\
  1704	  =& \sum_{g_X, g_Z} (-1)^{\tr( e_j(\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \\
  1705	  &\hspace{24em}\tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\alice ''} \\
  1706		 =& \sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \Big)_{\alice ''} \\
  1707		 =& \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \Big)_{\alice ''}\;,
  1708	\end{align*}
  1709	where in the third line we used the (anti-)commutation relation
  1710	\[
  1711		\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) = (-1)^{\tr( e_j(\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \;.
  1712	\]
  1713	An entirely analogous calculation shows that $V_\bob \, \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \, V_\bob^\dagger = \Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \Big( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \Big)_{\bob ''}$.
  1714	
  1715	Next, from the self-consistency property of the observables $\tilde{W}^j$ specified in \Cref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} we get that for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1716	\[
  1717		\E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \left ( \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \Id - \Id \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \right)^\dagger \left ( \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \Id - \Id \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \right) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \leq \delta_S\;,
  1718	\]
  1719	which, since $\tilde{W}^j$ is Hermitian, is equivalent to
  1720	\begin{equation}
  1721	\label{eq:qld-unitary-1}
  1722	\E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \geq 1 - \delta_S/2\;.
  1723	\end{equation}
  1724	Let $\ket{\vartheta} = V_\alice \otimes V_\bob \ket{\hat{\psi}}$, and for $W \in \{X,Z\}$ define the operator
  1725	\begin{align*}
  1726		H_W &= \E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \otimes \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \\
  1727			&= \E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \Big ( \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(e_j s) \otimes \tau^W(e_j s) \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits} \\
  1728			&= \Big ( \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(s) \otimes \tau^W(s) \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits}
  1729	\end{align*}
  1730	where in the second line we used that for all $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$, $\tau^W(\tilde{u}) = \bigotimes_{i = 1}^\nqubits \tau^W(\tilde{u}_i)$ with $\tau^W(\tilde{u}_i)$ being the generalized Pauli $W$ observable acting on the $i$-th qudit. In the third line, we used the fact that for every fixed $j$, we have $\E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(e_j s) \otimes \tau^W(e_j s) = \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(s) \otimes \tau^W(s)$. \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-1} is then equivalent to 
  1731	\[
  1732		\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - \delta_S/2\;,
  1733	\]
  1734	for $W \in \{X,Z\}$. 
  1735	
  1736	Observe that
  1737	\begin{align*}
  1738		\E_{s,s'} \tau^X(s) \tau^Z(s') \otimes \tau^X(s) \tau^Z(s') &= \E_{s,s'} \sum_{a,b \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(as')} \ketbra{a+s}{a} \otimes (-1)^{\tr(bs')} \ketbra{b+s}{b} \\
  1739		&= \E_{s} \sum_{a\in \F_q} \ketbra{a+s}{a} \otimes \ketbra{a+s}{a} \\
  1740		&= \proj{\EPR_q}
  1741	\end{align*}
  1742	where to go from the first to the second line we used \Cref{lem:cancellation}. This implies that $H_X H_Z = \Big ( \E_{s,s' \in \F_q} \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') \otimes \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits} = \ketbra{\EPR_q}{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$.
  1743	By the triangle inequality, we have
  1744	\[
  1745		\left \| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\| \leq \left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_X \ket{\vartheta} \right\| + \left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\|\;.
  1746	\]
  1747	Note that for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1748	\[
  1749		\left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_W \ket{\vartheta} \right\|^2 = 1 - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} + \bra{\vartheta} H_W^2 \ket{\vartheta} \leq 2 - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} \leq \delta_S\;,
  1750	\]
  1751	where in the inequality we used that $H_W \leq \Id$. Furthermore,
  1752	\begin{align*}
  1753		\bra{\vartheta} H_W^2 \ket{\vartheta} &=\| H_W \ket{\vartheta} \|^2\\
  1754		 &= \| \ket{\vartheta} + (H_W - \Id) \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \\
  1755		 &\geq (\|\ket{\vartheta}\| - \| (H_W - \Id) \ket{\vartheta} \|)^2 \\
  1756		 &\geq (1 - \delta_S)^2 \\
  1757		 &\geq 1 - 2\delta_S\;. 
  1758	\end{align*}
  1759	Therefore 
  1760	\begin{align*}
  1761	2\sqrt{\delta_S} &\geq \left \| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\|^2  \\
  1762	&= \bra{\vartheta} H_X^2 \ket{\vartheta} + \bra{\vartheta} H_Z^2 \ket{\vartheta} - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_X H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \\
  1763	&\geq 2 - 4\delta_S - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_X H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \;,
  1764	\end{align*}
  1765	which implies that 
  1766	\[
  1767		\bra{\vartheta} (\Id_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes (\proj{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''}) \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - 2\delta_S - \sqrt{\delta_S} \;.
  1768	\]
  1769	Define the unnormalized state $\ket{\aux_0}$ on the registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ as
  1770	\[
  1771		\ket{\aux_0}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} = (\bra{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''} \cdot \ket{\vartheta}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''}
  1772	\]
  1773	and define the normalized state $\ket{\aux} = \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \ket{\aux_0}$. 
  1774	The inner product between $\ket{\vartheta}$ and $\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$ can thus be evaluated as
  1775	\begin{align*}
  1776		\bra{\vartheta} (\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}) &= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \bra{\vartheta} (\ket{\aux_0} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}) \\
  1777		&= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \bra{\vartheta} (\Id_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes (\proj{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''}) \ket{\vartheta} \\
  1778		&= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|^2 \\
  1779		&= \| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \| \\
  1780		&\geq \sqrt{1 - 2\delta_S - \sqrt{\delta_S}} \\
  1781		&\geq 1 - O(\sqrt{\delta_S})\;.
  1782	\end{align*}
  1783	This implies $\| \ket{\vartheta} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$, which establishes the first item of the lemma.
  1784	
  1785	We now establish the second item of the lemma. In what follows, all $\simeq$ and $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$. From \Cref{lem:qld-win-implications} we have the following implications: for all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and on average over $u \in \F_q^m$,
  1786		\begin{align}
  1787		\label{eq:qld-unitary-2}
  1788		M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} &\simeq_\eps \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a\;, \\
  1789		\label{eq:qld-unitary-3}
  1790		\Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a &\simeq_\eps  M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''}\;,
  1791		\end{align}
  1792		where $M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \sum_{h : g_h(u) = a} M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h$. 
  1793	From \Cref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} we get that
  1794		\begin{equation}
  1795		\label{eq:qld-unitary-4}
  1796			M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \simeq_{\delta_S} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''}  \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a\;.
  1797		\end{equation}
  1798	Using \Cref{fact:triangle-for-simeq} with Equations \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-2}, \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-3}, and \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-4}, we get 
  1799		\begin{equation}
  1800			\label{eq:qld-unitary-5}
  1801			M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \simeq_{\sqrt{\delta_S}} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''}  \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a\;,
  1802		\end{equation}
  1803		where we used that $\delta_S \geq \eps$. 
  1804		
  1805		Next, we have for all $u \in \F_q^m$ 
  1806		\begin{align}
  1807			&V_\bob \, \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \, V_\bob^\dagger \notag \\
  1808			= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W_{g_W(u) - a}(\ind_m(u))    \tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1809			= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a} \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W_h   \tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1810			= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a} \Big ( \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)}   \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1811		= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \sum_{h : g_h(u) = a} \Big ( \tau^W_{h}   \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1812	= &\Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]})_{\bob''}\;,		\label{eq:qld-unitary-6}
  1813		\end{align}
  1814		where in the second line we expanded out the definitions of $V_\bob$ and $\tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a$ (defined in \cref{eq:tilde_M}); in the third line we expanded out the definition of $\tau^W_{g_W(u) - a}(\ind_m(u))$ (defined in \cref{eq:def-tauwu}) and used the fact that for all $h \in \F_q^M$, the inner product $h \cdot \ind_m(u)$ is equal to $g_h(u)$; in the fourth line we used the identities
  1815		\[
  1816			\tau^X(s) \tau^Z_h \tau^X(s)^\dagger = \tau^Z_{h + s} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \tau^Z(s) \tau^X_h \tau^Z(s)^\dagger = \tau^X_{h + s}~;
  1817		\]
  1818		and in the fifth line is due to the following short calculation: for all fixed $g_W$ we have
  1819		\begin{align*}
  1820			\sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a}  \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h: g_W(u) - g_h(u) = a} \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h: g_W(u) + g_h(u) = a} \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h': g_{h'}(u) = a} \tau^W_{h'}~.
  1821		\end{align*}
  1822		The second equality from the fact that $\F_q$ is a field of characteristic $2$ (so subtraction is the same as addition), and the third equality follows from the fact that letting $h' = h + \coded(g_W)$, we have $g_{h'} = g_h + g_W$ (in other words, the low-degree encoding $h \mapsto g_h$ is linear in $h$). 
  1823		
  1824		
  1825	
  1826	
  1827	Let $\ket{\Delta} = \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$. We show that $V_\alice \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \Big)_{\alice} \, V_\alice^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''}$ (the argument for the operators acting on registers $\bob \bob' \bob''$ proceeds identically). 
  1828		\begin{align}
  1829			&\sum_h \bra{\Delta} \left ( V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger - (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''}  \right)^\dagger \left ( V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger - (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \right) \ket{\Delta} \notag \\
  1830			&= 2 - 2 \Re \, \sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_\alice\, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \ket{\Delta} \notag \\
  1831			&= 2 - 2 \, \sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-7}
  1832	\end{align}
  1833		where in the last line we used that $(\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} = (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$.
  1834		We now claim that
  1835		\begin{align}
  1836		&  \, \sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta}  \notag \\
  1837		&\approx_{md/q}  \E_u \sum_{\substack{h, h' : \\ g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)}} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-8} \\
  1838		&=  \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \, V_\alice^\dagger \, \otimes (\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \notag \\
  1839		&=  \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \, V_\alice^\dagger \, \otimes V_\bob  \, \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \, V_\bob^\dagger \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-9}
  1840		\end{align}
  1841		where the equality in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-9} follows from the identity in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-6}, and the approximation in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-8} follows from the following calculation:
  1842		\begin{align*}
  1843			& \E_u \sum_{\substack{h \neq h' : \\ g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)}} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta}  \\
  1844			&= \sum_{h \neq h'} \left( \E_u \mathbf{1}[g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)] \right) \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \\
  1845			&\leq \frac{md}{q}\;.
  1846		\end{align*}
  1847		In the last line we used that for for distinct $h \neq h'$, the polynomials $g_h \neq g_{h'}$ and thus by the Schwartz-Zippel lemma can only agree on at most $md/q$ fraction of points $u \in \F_q^m$. 
  1848		
  1849		Continuing from \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-9}, we use the first item of the Lemma which shows that $\| \ket{\Delta} - \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$ and equivalently $\| V_\alice^\dagger \otimes V_\bob^\dagger \ket{\Delta} - \ket{\hat{\psi}} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$, so 
  1850		\begin{align*}
  1851			\text{\cref{eq:qld-unitary-9}} &\approx_{O(\delta_S^{1/4})} \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\hat{\psi}} M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1852			&\geq 1 - O(\delta_S^{1/2})\;,
  1853		\end{align*}
  1854	        where the last line comes from \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-5}.
  1855		Together with \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-7}, 
  1856		\[
  1857		\text{\cref{eq:qld-unitary-7}} \leq O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)\;.	
  1858		\]
  1859		This concludes the proof of the second item of the lemma.
  1860	\end{proof}
  1861	
  1862	We now prove \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}. 
  1863	\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}]
  1864		Let $\strategy = (\psi,M)$ be a projective strategy for $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeeds with probability at least $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi}$ is a bipartite state on registers $\alice \bob$. As mentioned at the beginning of \Cref{sec:commutation}, we assume that the state $\ket{\psi}$ is padded with sufficiently many ancilla $\ket{0}$ qubits. Let $\phi_\alice$ be the following isometry mapping the register $\alice$ to the registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ where $\alice'$ and $\alice''$ are isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$:
  1865		\[
  1866			\phi_\alice: \ket{\theta}_\alice \mapsto V_\alice (\ket{\theta}_\alice \otimes (\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice' \alice''})
  1867		\]
  1868		where $V_\alice$ is the unitary acting on $\alice \alice' \alice''$ from \Cref{lem:qld-unitary}. Define the isometry $\phi_\bob$ analogously. \Cref{lem:qld-unitary} then implies that there exists a state $\ket{\aux}$ on registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ such that
  1869		\[
  1870			\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_\bob \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} \right \|^2 \leq \delta_\qld
  1871		\]
  1872		and for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1873		\[
  1874			\phi_\alice \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\alice \, \phi_\alice^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \phi_\bob \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\bob \, \phi_\bob^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''}
  1875		\]
  1876		where the $\approx$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$. This shows that $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ is a self-test for the strategy $\strategy^\pauli$ with robustness $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)$. We conclude the proof by making the identification of registers $\alice \alice'$ with $\alice'$ and $\bob \bob'$ with $\bob'$ to be consistent with the statement of \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}. We also note that, when unpacking the dependence on parameters $\eps, m, d, q$, the function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)$ has the form $a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for some universal constants $a > 1, 0 < b < 1$, as desired.
  1877	\end{proof}

    41	  have hv : pauliProj .Z (0 : ι → K) v v = if v = 0 then 1 else 0 := by

    43	      star (∏ i, if v i = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0) = _
    44	    simp only [Fintype.prod_boole, ← funext_iff]
    45	    change (if v = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0) * star (if v = 0 then 1 else 0) = _

   155	        ‖applyOperatorToState (U u) ψ‖ :=
   156	      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (norm_sum_le _ _) (norm_nonneg _)
   157	    _ = ‖ψ‖ := by
   158	      simp only [hnorm, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul]
   159	      rw [norm_inv, Complex.norm_natCast, ← mul_assoc, inv_mul_cancel₀, one_mul]
   160	      positivity

   162	/-- Near-perfect X and Z correlations force proximity to the EPR subspace.
   163	This is the corrected projection estimate for paper lines 1743-1767, with
   164	arbitrary auxiliary registers. It uses the product identity and contraction
   165	bounds, and avoids the invalid squared-triangle estimate in the source. -/
   166	theorem norm_sub_eprProjection_le {R : Type*} [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
   167	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (R × ((ι → K) × (ι → K)))) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1)
   168	    (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
   169	    (hcorr : ∀ W : PauliKind,
   170	      1 - δ / 2 ≤ (inner ℂ ψ
   171	        (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (1 : Op R) (pauliCorrelation W)) ψ)).re) :
   172	    ‖ψ - applyOperatorToState
   173	      (heteroKron (1 : Op R) (Matrix.vecMulVec (fun x => eprState (ι → K) x)
   174	        (fun y => star (eprState (ι → K) y)))) ψ‖ ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt δ := by
   175	  let H (W : PauliKind) := heteroKron (1 : Op R) (pauliCorrelation (K := K) (ι := ι) W)
   176	  have hdist (W : PauliKind) : ‖ψ - applyOperatorToState (H W) ψ‖ ≤ Real.sqrt δ := by
   177	    have hn := norm_heteroKron_pauliCorrelation_apply_le W ψ
   178	    rw [hψ] at hn
   179	    have hs : ‖applyOperatorToState (H W) ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤ 1 := by
   180	      dsimp only [H]
   181	      nlinarith [norm_nonneg (applyOperatorToState (H W) ψ)]
   182	    have he := norm_sub_sq (𝕜 := ℂ) ψ (applyOperatorToState (H W) ψ)
   183	    rw [hψ] at he
   184	    change ‖ψ - applyOperatorToState (H W) ψ‖ ^ 2 =
   185	      1 ^ 2 - 2 * (inner ℂ ψ (applyOperatorToState (H W) ψ)).re +
   186	        ‖applyOperatorToState (H W) ψ‖ ^ 2 at he
   187	    have hc := hcorr W
   188	    change 1 - δ / 2 ≤ (inner ℂ ψ (applyOperatorToState (H W) ψ)).re at hc
   189	    nlinarith [Real.sq_sqrt hδ, Real.sqrt_nonneg δ,
   190	      norm_nonneg (ψ - applyOperatorToState (H W) ψ)]
   191	  have hprod : H .X * H .Z =
   192	      heteroKron (1 : Op R) (Matrix.vecMulVec (fun x => eprState (ι → K) x)
   193	        (fun y => star (eprState (ι → K) y))) := by
   194	    dsimp only [H]
   195	    rw [heteroKron_mul, Matrix.one_mul, pauliCorrelation_mul_eq_epr]
   196	  rw [← hprod, DistanceCalculus.applyOperatorToState_mul]
   197	  calc
   198	    _ ≤ ‖ψ - applyOperatorToState (H .X) ψ‖ +
   199	        ‖applyOperatorToState (H .X) ψ -
   200	          applyOperatorToState (H .X) (applyOperatorToState (H .Z) ψ)‖ :=
   201	      norm_sub_le_norm_sub_add_norm_sub _ _ _
   202	    _ ≤ Real.sqrt δ + Real.sqrt δ := add_le_add (hdist .X) (by
   203	      rw [← MagicSquareRigidity.applyOperatorToState_sub]
   204	      exact (norm_heteroKron_pauliCorrelation_apply_le .X _).trans (hdist .Z))
   205	    _ = 2 * Real.sqrt δ := by ring
   206	
   207	end

    25	/-- Move each extracted register before its auxiliary registers. This
    26	permutation puts the ideal state in the order used by
    27	`MagicSquareRigidity.exists_unit_residual`. -/
    28	def extractionEprFirstEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :
    29	    SixReg P ιA ιB ≃
    30	      (PauliRegister P × (ιA × PauliRegister P)) ×
    31	        (PauliRegister P × (ιB × PauliRegister P)) :=
    32	  (sixRegExtractionEquiv P ιA ιB).trans

    37	/-- Partial inner product with the EPR vector, leaving the auxiliary index.
    38	This is the coordinate form of the vector defined at paper line 1769. -/
    39	def eprPartialInner {R V : Type*} [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
    40	    [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V]
    41	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (R × (V × V))) : EuclideanSpace ℂ R :=
    42	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv R ℂ).symm
    43	    (fun r => ∑ p : V × V, star (eprState V p) * ψ (r, p))
    44	
    45	/-- Tensoring the EPR partial inner product with EPR gives the rank-one
    46	projection on the second tensor factor. This is the projection equality in
    47	paper lines 1776-1779; no normalization of the auxiliary vector is assumed. -/
    48	theorem vecTensor_eprPartialInner {R V : Type*} [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
    49	    [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V]
    50	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (R × (V × V))) :
    51	    vecTensor (eprPartialInner ψ) (eprState V) =
    52	      applyOperatorToState
    53	        (heteroKron (1 : Op R) (Matrix.vecMulVec (fun x => eprState V x)
    54	          (fun y => star (eprState V y)))) ψ := by
    55	  ext x
    56	  change (∑ p : V × V, star (eprState V p) * ψ (x.1, p)) * eprState V x.2 =
    57	    ∑ j : R × (V × V),
    58	      ((1 : Op R) x.1 j.1 * (eprState V x.2 * star (eprState V j.2))) * ψ j
    59	  conv_rhs => rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
    60	  simp only [Matrix.one_apply, ite_mul, one_mul, zero_mul]
    61	  conv_rhs => rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    62	  simp only [Finset.sum_ite_eq, Finset.mem_univ, ite_true]
    63	  rw [Finset.sum_mul]
    64	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    65	  intro p _
    66	  ring
    67	
    68	end Extraction

   128	theorem idealExpState_extractionAux0
   129	    (θ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
   130	    S.idealExpState (S.extractionAux0 θ) =
   131	      applyOperatorToState S.extractionEprProjection θ := by
   132	  unfold idealExpState extractionAux0
   133	  rw [Extraction.vecTensor_eprPartialInner]
   134	  ext x
   135	  let e := (extractionIdealShuffle P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB).symm
   136	  let T := heteroKron
   137	    (1 : Op (ExtractionAuxRegisters P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB))

   141	    ((T.submatrix e e) *ᵥ (fun j => θ j)) x
   142	  exact (congrFun (Matrix.submatrix_mulVec_equiv T (fun j => θ j) e e) x).symm

   148	theorem exists_unit_aux_near_eprProjection
   149	    (θ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)) (hθ : ‖θ‖ = 1) :

    43	theorem exists_pulled_apart_consistency :

+theorem exists_pulled_apart_consistency :
+    ∃ a b C : ℝ, 1 < a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧ 1 ≤ C ∧
+      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (epsilon : ℝ),
+        0 ≤ epsilon → epsilon ≤ 1 → ∀ S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon,
+          ∃ w : GlobalPairWitness S (deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q),

+                    (deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q) P.m P.d P.q ∧

+                  (fun u r => S.placePlayer .bob ((S.pointMeas .bob W u).effect r))
+                  S.psiHat ≤ deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon
+                    (deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q) P.m P.d P.q ∧
+              ∀ j : Fin P.model.basisDim,

+                    (fun u => S.placeSide .alice (tildeObs w .alice W u j))
+                    (fun u => S.placeSide .bob (tildeObs w .bob W u j))
+                    S.psiHat ≤ deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon

+end

  1463	\begin{lemma}
  1464	  \label{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis}
  1465	Let $\delta_S$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}.
  1466	For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, all $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$ and $j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}$, the measurements $\{ \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \}_{a \in \F_q}$ and observables $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$ satisfy the following properties:
  1467	\begin{enumerate}
  1468	\item (\textbf{Consistency with points measurements}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, for all $j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}$, and on average over uniformly random $u \in \F_q^m$,
  1469		\[
  1470			\Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \simeq_{\delta_S} M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''}
  1471		\]
  1472		and
  1473		\[
  1474			\tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \simeq_{\delta_S} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \;.

  1477		\[
  1478			\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \approx_{\delta_S} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})\,.
  1479		\]

  1483	\begin{proof}
  1484	We show the first item of the lemma for the case when $M^{(\Point,W),u}_a$ acts on register $\alice$ and $\tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a$ acts on registers $\bob \bob' \bob''$ (the argument for when the $\alice$ and $\bob$ registers are interchanged proceeds analogously):
  1485		\begin{align*}
  1486			&\E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_a \bra{\hat{\psi}} M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1487			&= \E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_{g,a} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (M^{(\Point,W),u}_a)_{\alice} \otimes (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_{\coded(g) \cdot \ind_m(u) -a}(\ind_m(u)))_{\bob''} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1488			&= \E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_{g} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{\coded(g) \cdot \ind_m(u)})_{\alice \bob''} \otimes (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\bob \bob'} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1489			&= \E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_{g} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{g(u)})_{\alice \bob''} \otimes (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\bob \bob'} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1490			&\geq 1 - \delta_S\;.
  1491		\end{align*}
  1492		The second line follows from expanding the definition of $\tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a$ using~\eqref{eq:tilde_M}, the third line follows from the definition of $\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a$ given in Section~\ref{sec:expanding}, the fourth line follows from the fact that $\coded(g) \cdot \ind_m(u) = g(u)$, and the fifth line follows from \Cref{lem:qld-4-7}. This implies the first item of the Lemma.

  1495	To show the second item we first argue that, on average over $\tilde{u}$, 
  1496		\begin{equation}
  1497			\label{eq:qld-pulling-cons}

  1501		\begin{align}
  1502			&\Big ( \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \Big)_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \label{eq:qld-pulling-0} \\
  1503			\approx_{\delta_S}& \Big ( \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \Big)_{\alice \alice'\alice''} \cdot \Big ( \sum_g (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes  (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{g(u)})_{\bob \alice''} \Big) \label{eq:qld-pulling-1} \\
  1504			=_{\phantom{\delta_S}}& \sum_g \Big ( (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_{(\coded(g) \cdot \tilde{u}) - a}(\tilde{u}))_{\alice''} \Big) \cdot \Big(\sum_{r,s: r + s = g(u)} (M^{(\Point,W),u}_r)_{\bob} \otimes (\tau_s^W(\ind_m(u)))_{\alice''} \Big) \label{eq:qld-pulling-2} \\
  1505			=_{\phantom{\delta_S}}& \sum_{\substack{g,h: \\ (\coded(g)-h)\cdot \tilde{u} = a}}  (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \otimes (M^{(\Point,W),u}_{(g-g_h)(u)})_{\bob}~. \label{eq:qld-pulling-2b}

  1651	The first inequality follows from the fact that $\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]} \leq \Id$ for all $a$, and the second inequality follows from the self-consistency of $\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a}$ (established in \Cref{lem:qld-comm-cons}). Thus
  1652	\[

  1655	On the other hand, notice that
  1656	\begin{align*}

  1658		=& \E_u \sum_g \bra{\hat{\psi}} ((\Id - \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{g(u)}) \cdot \hat{S}^W_{g} \cdot (\Id - \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{g(u)}))_{\alice \alice'} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1659		=& \E_u \sum_a \bra{\hat{\psi}} ((\Id - \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a}) \cdot \hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]} \cdot (\Id - \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a}))_{\alice \alice'} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1660		\leq& O(\delta_S + \eps).

  1662	\Cref{eq:qld-sg-cons2} is thus obtained by absorbing $\eps$ into the function $\delta_S$.  
  1663	\end{proof}

  1669	\begin{lemma}
  1670	\label{lem:qld-unitary}

  1672	\begin{enumerate}

  1674		\[
  1675			\left \| V_\alice \otimes V_\bob \ket{\hat{\psi}}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''} - \ket{\aux}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\alice'' \bob''} \right \|^2 \leq \delta_\qld.
  1676		\]
  1677		
  1678		\item For all $W \in \{X,Z\}, h \in \F_q^\nqubits$
  1679		\begin{align*}
  1680			V_\alice \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \Big)_{\alice} \, V_\alice^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \\
  1681			 V_\bob \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h  \Big)_{\bob}\, V_\bob^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''}
  1682		\end{align*}

  1687	\begin{proof}

  1689	Define the linear map
  1690	\[
  1691		V_\alice = \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)))_{\alice ''}\;,
  1692	\]

  1696		&= \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Id_{\alice ''} \\
  1697		&= \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''}

  1699	where in the first line we used that the measurement $\{ \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \}$  is projective and in the second line we used that the $\tau^Z$ and $\tau^X$ observables are self-inverse. The unitary $V_\bob$ is defined analogously.
  1700	
  1701	Let $\{e_j\}_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}}$ denote the self-dual basis for $\F_q$ over $\F_2$ specified in \Cref{sec:subfields}, and let $\tilde{W}^j$ be the observables introduced in~\eqref{eq:def-tildewj}.   1702	\begin{align*}
  1703		&V_\alice \, \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \, V_\alice^\dagger \\
  1704	  =& \sum_{g_X, g_Z} (-1)^{\tr( e_j(\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \\
  1705	  &\hspace{24em}\tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\alice ''} \\

  1707		 =& \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \Big)_{\alice ''}\;,
  1708	\end{align*}
  1709	where in the third line we used the (anti-)commutation relation
  1710	\[
  1711		\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) = (-1)^{\tr( e_j(\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \;.
  1712	\]

  1714	
  1715	Next, from the self-consistency property of the observables $\tilde{W}^j$ specified in \Cref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} we get that for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1716	\[
  1717		\E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \left ( \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \Id - \Id \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \right)^\dagger \left ( \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \Id - \Id \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \right) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \leq \delta_S\;,
  1718	\]

  1720	\begin{equation}
  1721	\label{eq:qld-unitary-1}
  1722	\E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \geq 1 - \delta_S/2\;.
  1723	\end{equation}
  1724	Let $\ket{\vartheta} = V_\alice \otimes V_\bob \ket{\hat{\psi}}$, and for $W \in \{X,Z\}$ define the operator
  1725	\begin{align*}
  1726		H_W &= \E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \otimes \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \\
  1727			&= \E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \Big ( \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(e_j s) \otimes \tau^W(e_j s) \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits} \\
  1728			&= \Big ( \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(s) \otimes \tau^W(s) \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits}

  1730	where in the second line we used that for all $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$, $\tau^W(\tilde{u}) = \bigotimes_{i = 1}^\nqubits \tau^W(\tilde{u}_i)$ with $\tau^W(\tilde{u}_i)$ being the generalized Pauli $W$ observable acting on the $i$-th qudit.   1731	\[

  1734	for $W \in \{X,Z\}$. 
  1735	
  1736	Observe that
  1737	\begin{align*}
  1738		\E_{s,s'} \tau^X(s) \tau^Z(s') \otimes \tau^X(s) \tau^Z(s') &= \E_{s,s'} \sum_{a,b \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(as')} \ketbra{a+s}{a} \otimes (-1)^{\tr(bs')} \ketbra{b+s}{b} \\

  1742	where to go from the first to the second line we used \Cref{lem:cancellation}. This implies that $H_X H_Z = \Big ( \E_{s,s' \in \F_q} \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') \otimes \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits} = \ketbra{\EPR_q}{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$.
  1743	By the triangle inequality, we have
  1744	\[
  1745		\left \| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\| \leq \left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_X \ket{\vartheta} \right\| + \left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\|\;.
  1746	\]
  1747	Note that for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1748	\[
  1749		\left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_W \ket{\vartheta} \right\|^2 = 1 - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} + \bra{\vartheta} H_W^2 \ket{\vartheta} \leq 2 - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} \leq \delta_S\;,

  1751	where in the inequality we used that $H_W \leq \Id$. Furthermore,
  1752	\begin{align*}

  1770	\[
  1771		\ket{\aux_0}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} = (\bra{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''} \cdot \ket{\vartheta}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''}

1	# Mathematical Language Guidelines
     2	
     3	MIPStarRE Lean names and documentation should be written for readers comparing
     4	the formalization with the paper and blueprint.
     5	
     6	This is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,
     7	naming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,
     8	`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.
     9	
    10	## Scope
    11	
    12	These guidelines apply to:
    13	
    14	- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;
    15	- module docstrings;
    16	- declaration docstrings;
    17	- documentation-visible section comments;
    18	- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.
    19	- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;
    20	- issue titles and issue bodies;
    21	- PR titles and PR descriptions.
    22	
    23	## Source of Truth
    24	
    25	Use terminology from the following sources, in this order:
    26	
    27	1. `references/ldt-paper/`
    28	2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`
    29	3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files
    30	
    31	When the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for
    32	example, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to
    33	projectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.
    34	
    35	## Reference Notation And Terminology
    36	
    37	The notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for
    38	reader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean
    39	docstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source
    40	without first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.
    41	
    42	When Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a
    43	location which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the
    44	first applicable location in the following order:
    45	
    46	1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation
    47	   differs from the paper;
    48	2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a
    49	   family of declarations in that file;
    50	3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the
    51	   blueprint;
    52	4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a
    53	   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.
    54	
    55	The explanation should say:
    56	
    57	- the notation or term used in the paper;
    58	- the Lean object or name which represents it;
    59	- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;
    60	- the scope in which the replacement should be used.
    61	
    62	A PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place
    63	where future readers can learn it.
    64	
    65	Formalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose
    66	should name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,
    67	rather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.
    68	
    69	## Naming Norm
    70	
    71	Names and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or
    72	conclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was
    73	assembled.
    74	
    75	Avoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,
    76	`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source
    77	uses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes
    78	such as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a
    79	clearer phrase.
    80	
    81	This is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.
    82	Module names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,
    83	blueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the
    84	mathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line
    85	number, or implementation history.
    86	
    87	### Concrete examples
    88	
    89	The table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the
    90	codebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;
    91	others are proposed names for future refactors.  The "avoid" column lists
    92	process-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was
    93	assembled; the "prefer" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the
    94	paper or blueprint would recognize.
    95	
    96	| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |
    97	|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
    98	| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not "the line-130 identity"          |
    99	| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |
   100	| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |
   101	| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |
   102	| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |
   103	| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |
   104	| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |
   105	| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
   106	| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
   107	| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |
   108	
   109	An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
   110	phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").
   111	In that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.
   112	
   113	File-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be
   114	named by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations
   115	exposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.
   116	
   117	### Shared helpers
   118	
   119	When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
   120	more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
   121	shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
   122	ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
   123	call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.
   124	
   125	Procedure:
   126	
   127	1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   128	   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   129	   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   130	   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   131	   explicit argument.
   132	2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   133	   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   134	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   135	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   136	   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
   137	3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   138	   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.
   139	4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace
   140	   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   141	   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   142	   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   143	   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   144	   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.
   145	5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or
   146	   blueprint location it supports.
   147	
   148	### Legacy identifier treatment
   149	
   150	If a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and
   151	describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
   152	identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
   153	in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.
   154	
   155	Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
   156	public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
   157	shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
   158	blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.
   159	
   160	## Review Checklist
   161	
   162	Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
   163	documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.
   164	
   165	- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
   166	      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,
   167	      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the
   168	      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,
   169	      implementation-phase labels)?
   170	- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does
   171	      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the
   172	      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,
   173	      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the
   174	      source does not use them that way?
   175	- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from
   176	      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,
   177	      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in
   178	      that order of preference?
   179	- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced
   180	      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or
   181	      construction they support?
   182	- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists
   183	      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been
   184	      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?
   185	- [ ] **Legacy IDs.**  If a legacy Lean identifier is mentioned, is the
   186	      mathematical object described in paper terminology?  If an old public
   187	      identifier cannot be renamed yet, is the required migration recorded in
   188	      the issue, PR description, or an audit file?
   189	- [ ] **Pass-through names.**  Does the PR add an empty pass-through
   190	      abbreviation that introduces a second public name without adding
   191	      mathematical content?  Reject it unless it is a documented compatibility
   192	      wrapper preserving paper-facing or blueprint-facing terminology.
   193	
   194	Review-fix PRs touching a surface covered by an active audit should read the
   195	relevant audit before changing names or prose.
   196	
   197	[#1145]: https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE/issues/1145

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:121:/-- Natural powers of a generalized Pauli observable multiply its label by

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:124:    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K]

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:127:      primeTauObservable (p := p) W (fun i => n • a i) := by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:128:  induction n with
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:129:  | zero =>
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:130:      rw [pow_zero]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:131:      have hzero : (fun i => (0 : ℕ) • a i) = (0 : ι → K) := by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:132:        funext i
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:133:        simp
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:134:      rw [hzero]

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:138:        (primeTauObservable (p := p) W a) ^ (n + 1) =
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:139:            (primeTauObservable (p := p) W a) ^ n *
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:140:              primeTauObservable (p := p) W a := pow_succ _ _

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:142:              primeTauObservable (p := p) W a := by rw [ih]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:143:        _ = primeTauObservable (p := p) W ((fun i => n • a i) + a) :=
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:144:              primeTauObservable_mul W _ _
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:145:        _ = primeTauObservable (p := p) W (fun i => (n + 1) • a i) := by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:146:              have hlabels : ((fun i => n • a i) + a) =
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:147:                  (fun i => (n + 1) • a i) := by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:148:                funext i
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:149:                rw [Pi.add_apply, add_nsmul, one_nsmul]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:150:              exact congrArg
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:151:                (fun c => primeTauObservable (p := p) W c) hlabels

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:155:theorem primeTauObservable_pow {p : ℕ} {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:156:    [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K] [Fintype ι]

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:261:theorem primeTauObservable_eigenvalue_pow_char {p : ℕ} {K ι : Type*}
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:262:    [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:263:    [Algebra (ZMod p) K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:264:    (W : Bool) (a : ι → K) (v : (ι → K) → ℂ) (eigenvalue : ℂ)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:265:    (hv : v ≠ 0)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:266:    (heigen : primeTauObservable (p := p) W a *ᵥ v = eigenvalue • v) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:267:    eigenvalue ^ p = 1 := by

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:269:      (primeTauObservable (p := p) W a) ^ n *ᵥ v = eigenvalue ^ n • v := by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:270:    induction n with
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:271:    | zero => simp
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:272:    | succ n ih =>

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:274:          pow_succ, smul_smul, mul_comm]

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:282:/-- A single-coordinate shift and phase satisfy the generalized Pauli twisted

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:284:private theorem primeTauShift_mul_primeTauPhase {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K]

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:289:        (primeTauPhase (p := p) b * primeTauShift (p := p) a) := by

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:291:  by_cases hxy : x = y + a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:292:  · subst x

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:294:      smul_eq_mul]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:295:    simp only [add_left_inj, mul_ite, ite_mul, one_mul, zero_mul, mul_zero,

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:299:    ring_nf
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:300:  · simp [Matrix.mul_apply, primeTauShift, primeTauPhase, Matrix.smul_apply, hxy]

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:302:/-- An additive character sends a finite sum to the product of its values. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:303:private theorem addChar_sum {A M ι : Type*} [AddCommMonoid A] [CommMonoid M]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:304:    [Fintype ι] (ψ : AddChar A M) (f : ι → A) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:305:    ψ (∑ i, f i) = ∏ i, ψ (f i) := by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:306:  classical
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:307:  induction (Finset.univ : Finset ι) using Finset.induction_on with
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:308:  | empty => simp
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:309:  | @insert i s hi ih =>
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:310:      rw [Finset.sum_insert hi, Finset.prod_insert hi, AddChar.map_add_eq_mul, ih]

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:315:    [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K] [Fintype ι]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:316:    [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι] (a b : ι → K) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:317:    primeTauObservable (p := p) true a * primeTauObservable (p := p) false b =
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:318:      (ffChar (p := p) (F := K) (-dotProduct a b)) •
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:319:        (primeTauObservable (p := p) false b * primeTauObservable (p := p) true a) := by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:320:  let ψ := ffChar (p := p) (F := K)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:321:  have hchar : ψ (-dotProduct a b) = ∏ i, ψ (-(a i) * b i) := by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:322:    calc
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:323:      ψ (-dotProduct a b) = ψ (∑ i, -(a i) * b i) := by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:324:        congr 1
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:325:        simp [dotProduct]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:326:      _ = ∏ i, ψ (-(a i) * b i) := addChar_sum ψ _

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:328:      productMatrix (fun i => primeTauPhase (p := p) (b i)) =
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:329:    ψ (-dotProduct a b) •
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:330:      (productMatrix (fun i => primeTauPhase (p := p) (b i)) *
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:331:        productMatrix (fun i => primeTauShift (p := p) (a i)))
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:332:  rw [productMatrix_mul, productMatrix_mul]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:333:  ext x y
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:334:  simp only [productMatrix, primeTauShift_mul_primeTauPhase, Matrix.smul_apply,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:335:    smul_eq_mul, Finset.prod_mul_distrib]

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:349:    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] [Algebra (ZMod 2) K] [Fintype ι]

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:351:    tauObservable W a = primeTauObservable (p := 2)

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:353:  cases W with
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:354:  | X =>
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:355:      ext x y

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:681:theorem pauliProj_reindex_quditQubitLabelEquiv
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:682:    {q : ℕ} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (F : FixedFieldModel q)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:683:    (W : PauliKind) (u : ι → F.K) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:684:    pauliProj W u =
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:685:      Matrix.reindex (quditQubitLabelEquiv F).symm
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:686:        (quditQubitLabelEquiv F).symm
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:687:        (pauliProj W (kappaVec F u)) := by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:688:  classical
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:689:  rw [pauliProj_eq_avg_tauObservable, pauliProj_eq_avg_tauObservable]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:690:  ext x y

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:693:  rw [Fintype.card_congr (quditQubitLabelEquiv (ι := ι) F)]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:694:  congr 1
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:695:  apply Fintype.sum_equiv (quditQubitLabelEquiv F)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:696:  intro a
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:697:  have hphase := congrArg phaseSign
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:698:    (binTrace_dotProduct_eq_quditQubitLabelEquiv F a u)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:699:  have hentry := congrFun
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:700:    (congrFun (tauObservable_reindex_quditQubitLabelEquiv F W a) x) y
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:701:  simp only [Matrix.reindex_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply, Equiv.symm_symm] at hentry
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:702:  rw [hphase, hentry]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:703:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:704:/-- The tensor product of binary Pauli projectors, obtained by specializing
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:705:`pauliProj` to `ZMod 2`. This is the binary target in blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:706:`lem:pauli-binary`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:707:`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1163-1208`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:708:noncomputable abbrev qubitPauliProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:709:    (W : PauliKind) (b : ι → ZMod 2) : Op (ι → ZMod 2) :=
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:710:  pauliProj W b
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:711:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:712:/-- `lem:pauli-binary`: the fixed binary coordinates induce an isometry that
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:713:maps EPR states and generalized Pauli projectors to their qubit forms.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:714:Blueprint `lem:pauli-binary`, paper
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:715:`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1163-1208`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:716:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:717:**Local fix:** The source's final factor index is printed as
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:718:`j ∈ {1, ..., q}`; the basis expansion at paper lines 1191--1194 shows that
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:719:the intended range has `basisDim = log₂ q` entries. This correction is
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:720:documented in `rem:pauli-binary-source` and issue #16. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:721:theorem exists_qubitIsometry (q : ℕ) (F : FixedFieldModel q) (L : ℕ) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:722:    ∃ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin L → F.K) ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:723:        EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin L × Fin F.basisDim → ZMod 2),
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:724:      isometryTensor φ.toLinearIsometry φ.toLinearIsometry
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:725:          (eprState (Fin L → F.K)) =
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:726:          eprState (Fin L × Fin F.basisDim → ZMod 2) ∧
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:727:        ∀ (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin L → F.K),
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:728:          pauliProj W u =
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:729:            conjIsometry φ.symm.toLinearIsometry
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:730:              (qubitPauliProj W (kappaVec F u)) := by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:731:  let e := quditQubitLabelEquiv (ι := Fin L) F
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:732:  let φ := LinearIsometryEquiv.piLpCongrLeft 2 ℂ ℂ e
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:733:  refine ⟨φ, isometryTensor_piLpCongrLeft_epr e, ?_⟩
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:734:  intro W u
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:735:  rw [conjIsometry_piLpCongrLeft_symm]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:736:  exact pauliProj_reindex_quditQubitLabelEquiv F W u
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:737:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/PauliTheorems.lean:738:end MIPStarRE.QPBT
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:1:import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Algebra.Decoding
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:2:import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Observables.ExpandedDefs

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:4:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:5:/-! # Encoding-supported Pauli reference measurements
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:6:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:7:The reference measurement measures the strategy's Pauli answer and an independent
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:8:ideal Pauli answer, then returns the bounded encoding of their sum. Its effects
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:9:vanish outside the encoding image. Evaluation of its polynomial outcome is the
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:10:convolution of the evaluated strategy measurement and the ideal point projectors.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:11:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:12:These are internal auxiliary constructions for blueprint `eq:qld-nonencoding-mass`
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:13:and `lem:qld-nonencoding-mass-bound`, not the quantitative support estimate. No
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:14:winning premise or global polynomial-pair witness is used or constructed here.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:15:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:16:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:17:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:18:The encoding is paper `eq:low-degree-encoding-definition` in
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:19:`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:882-897`. The convolution is the Pauli
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:20:answer replacement of the expanded point measurement at
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:21:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:383-418`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:22:The corrected use in `lem:qld-construct-the-paulis` is recorded in blueprint
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:23:`eq:qld-nonencoding-mass` and `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex`.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:24:-/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:25:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:26:open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:27:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:28:namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:29:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:30:open MIPStarRE.Quantum
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:31:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:32:variable {params : AdmissibleParams} {error : ℝ}
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:33:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:34:/-- The ideal Pauli basis measurement on the ancillary register, bundled using
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:35:positivity and completeness of the existing Pauli projectors. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:36:noncomputable def pauliRegisterMeas (basis : PauliKind) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:37:    Measurement (PauliRegister params) (PauliRegister params) :=
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:38:  Measurement.ofSumEqOne (pauliProj basis)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:39:    (fun answer => Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr (posSemidef_pauliProj basis answer))
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:40:    (sum_pauliProj_eq_one basis)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:41:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:42:/-- Every bounded encoding lies in the full-field decoder's encoding image. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:43:@[simp] theorem isEncoding_encodingPoly (answer : PauliRegister params) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:44:    IsEncoding (encodingPoly answer) := by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:45:  unfold IsEncoding
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:46:  rw [decodeFq_lowDegreeEncoding]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:47:  rfl
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:48:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:49:namespace ProjectiveSetting
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:50:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:51:/-- Measure the strategy Pauli answer and the ancillary ideal Pauli answer and
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:52:return the encoding of their sum. This complete POVM is the internal reference
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:53:measurement underlying blueprint `eq:qld-nonencoding-mass`; it is not the global
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:54:polynomial measurement whose existence is required in `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:55:noncomputable def encodingPauliMeas (setting : ProjectiveSetting params error)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:56:    (side : PlayerSide) (basis : PauliKind) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:57:    Measurement (Poly params) (setting.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:58:  (tensorMeasurement (setting.pauliMeas side basis) (pauliRegisterMeas basis)).postprocess
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:59:    fun answers => encodingPoly (answers.1 + answers.2)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:60:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:61:/-- The reference effect sums the product effects over pairs whose sum encodes
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:62:the specified polynomial representative. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:63:theorem encodingPauliMeas_effect (setting : ProjectiveSetting params error)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:64:    (side : PlayerSide) (basis : PauliKind) (poly : Poly params) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:65:    (setting.encodingPauliMeas side basis).effect poly =
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:66:      ∑ answers ∈ Finset.univ.filter
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:67:          (fun answers : PauliRegister params × PauliRegister params =>
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:68:            encodingPoly (answers.1 + answers.2) = poly),
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:69:        heteroKron ((setting.pauliMeas side basis).effect answers.1)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:70:          (pauliProj basis answers.2) :=
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:71:  rfl
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:72:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:73:/-- Positivity is preserved by the tensor product and the encoding postprocessing. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:74:theorem encodingPauliMeas_effect_nonneg (setting : ProjectiveSetting params error)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:75:    (side : PlayerSide) (basis : PauliKind) (poly : Poly params) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:76:    0 ≤ (setting.encodingPauliMeas side basis).effect poly :=
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:77:  (setting.encodingPauliMeas side basis).pos poly
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:78:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:79:/-- The reference effects sum to the identity on the strategy and ancillary registers. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:80:theorem sum_encodingPauliMeas_effect_eq_one (setting : ProjectiveSetting params error)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:81:    (side : PlayerSide) (basis : PauliKind) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:82:    ∑ poly, (setting.encodingPauliMeas side basis).effect poly = 1 :=
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:83:  (setting.encodingPauliMeas side basis).sum_eq_one
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:84:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:85:/-- A nonencoding polynomial has zero reference effect. This is exact support of
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:86:the auxiliary measurement, not a bound on the global polynomial measurement. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:87:theorem encodingPauliMeas_effect_eq_zero_of_not_isEncoding
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:88:    (setting : ProjectiveSetting params error) (side : PlayerSide) (basis : PauliKind)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:89:    (poly : Poly params) (hpoly : ¬ IsEncoding poly) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:90:    (setting.encodingPauliMeas side basis).effect poly = 0 := by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:91:  classical
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:92:  rw [encodingPauliMeas_effect]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:93:  apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:94:  intro answers hanswers
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:95:  exact False.elim (hpoly ((Finset.mem_filter.mp hanswers).2 ▸
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:96:    isEncoding_encodingPoly (answers.1 + answers.2)))
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:97:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:98:/-- Evaluating the reference polynomial is equivalent to evaluating the two Pauli
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:99:answers separately and adding their values. This uses linearity of the encoding,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:100:not the decoder/evaluation identity for arbitrary polynomial representatives. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:101:theorem encodingPauliMeas_postprocess_eval (setting : ProjectiveSetting params error)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:102:    (side : PlayerSide) (basis : PauliKind) (point : Fin params.m → PauliScalar params) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:103:    (setting.encodingPauliMeas side basis).postprocess (fun poly => evalPoly poly point) =
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:104:      (tensorMeasurement (setting.pauliEvalMeas side basis point)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:105:        ((pauliRegisterMeas basis).postprocess
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:106:          (fun answer => lowDegreeEnc answer point))).postprocess
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:107:        (fun values => values.1 + values.2) := by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:108:  unfold encodingPauliMeas pauliEvalMeas
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:109:  rw [Measurement.postprocess_comp, tensorMeasurement_postprocess,
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:110:    Measurement.postprocess_comp]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:111:  apply congrArg ((tensorMeasurement (setting.pauliMeas side basis)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:112:    (pauliRegisterMeas basis)).postprocess)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:113:  funext answers
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:114:  change lowDegreeEnc (answers.1 + answers.2) point =
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:115:    lowDegreeEnc answers.1 point + lowDegreeEnc answers.2 point
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:116:  simp only [lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct, add_dotProduct]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:117:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:118:/-- The evaluated reference effects are exactly the Pauli-answer convolution
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:119:`K^u_a` in the proof of blueprint `eq:qld-nonencoding-mass`. This identity makes no
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:120:approximation or assertion of consistency with the strategy's point measurement. -/
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:121:theorem encodingPauliMeas_eval_effect_eq_convolution
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:122:    (setting : ProjectiveSetting params error) (side : PlayerSide) (basis : PauliKind)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:123:    (point : Fin params.m → PauliScalar params) (value : PauliScalar params) :
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:124:    ((setting.encodingPauliMeas side basis).postprocess
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:125:      (fun poly => evalPoly poly point)).effect value =
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:126:      ∑ values ∈ Finset.univ.filter
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:127:          (fun values : PauliScalar params × PauliScalar params => values.1 + values.2 = value),
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:128:        heteroKron ((setting.pauliEvalMeas side basis point).effect values.1)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:129:          (tauPointProj basis point values.2) := by
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:130:  rw [encodingPauliMeas_postprocess_eval, Measurement.postprocess_effect]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:131:  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:132:  intro values _
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:133:  change heteroKron ((setting.pauliEvalMeas side basis point).effect values.1)
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:134:    (((pauliRegisterMeas basis).postprocess
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:135:      (fun answer => lowDegreeEnc answer point)).effect values.2) = _
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:136:  simp only [Measurement.postprocess_effect, lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct]
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:137:  rfl
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:138:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:139:end ProjectiveSetting
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:140:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/EncodingSupport.lean:141:end MIPStarRE.QPBT

MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/PolynomialCollision.lean:4:/-!
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/PolynomialCollision.lean:5:# Real polynomial collision bounds
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/PolynomialCollision.lean:6:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/PolynomialCollision.lean:7:The existing Schwartz–Zippel estimate for bounded polynomial representatives
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/PolynomialCollision.lean:8:is expressed as a nonnegative rational cardinality ratio. This module converts
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/PolynomialCollision.lean:9:it to the real uniform average used by the sandwich support comparison and
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/PolynomialCollision.lean:10:specializes it to the polynomial outcomes of the Pauli basis test.
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/PolynomialCollision.lean:11:
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/PolynomialCollision.lean:12:## References
MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/PolynomialCollision.lean:13:
